attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post. He paraphrases LeCun, but the judgement that LeCun was wrong (that AI misinformation gained traction) is Marcus's own claim.

semantics.note: This is a retrospective observation that AI-generated misinformation had gained traction by April 2024. Marcus's paraphrase widens LeCun's point, which was about scientific misinformation, but the normalised claim keeps the core of what Marcus asserted.

contract.note: Marcus named no threshold. Reading 'traction' as wide spread or a real-world effect is an ordinary plain reading. Scoring part (b) and treating LeCun's tweets as context is fair. Under a narrower scientific-misinformation reading the result could differ.

evidence.note: LeCun's Nov 2022 tweet gives near-zero odds that auto-generated scientific misinformation has impact. Marcus's paraphrase holds in substance but is broader than LeCun's scope. This is a primary tweet, not a secondary summary.
LeCun's tweet says spreading misinformation and getting it believed are the main hurdles. This shows what he was arguing.
May 2023: an apparently AI-made image of a fake Pentagon explosion spread on Twitter and briefly moved markets. This is clear spread with a measurable effect.
Jan 2024: an apparently AI-generated Biden voice was used in robocalls to suppress voting, prompting a state AG investigation. The source does not quantify reach.
Apr 2024: X's trending Explore feature promoted a false headline apparently generated by Grok. This is platform-wide promotion, though reach is not quantified.

reviews.rationale: Between late 2022 and April 2024 there are dated, reputable reports of AI-generated false content that spread and had real effects. The Pentagon image moved markets, and the robocall and the Grok headline are further cases. This meets the support condition. LeCun did say something like what Marcus reports, but about scientific misinformation, so Marcus's paraphrase is broader. None of the cases is scientific misinformation.
